Fit Transmission Model Using PMCMC

fit_transmission_model.Rd

Runs a particle MCMC fit of the PREVAIL transmission model using pre-generated parameters and a serosurvey dataset. This function simulates two models (baseline and fitted) using the dust2 engine, and fits them using the monty framework. Parameter input should be generated externally using custom_data_process_wrapper.

Usage

fit_transmission_model(
  parameters,
  serodata,
  domain = matrix(c(0, 2, 0, 2), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
  vcv = diag(c(0.1, 0.1)),
  n_steps = 1000,
  n_chains = 1,
  n_particles = 1
)

Arguments

parameters

A named list of model parameters, as produced by custom_data_process_wrapper.

serodata

A data.frame with columns time and serosurvey, where serosurvey is a list-column containing numeric vectors of observed seropositivity by age.

domain

A 2-row matrix specifying the lower and upper bounds for each parameter. Default is matrix(c(0, 2, 0, 2), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE).

vcv

A variance-covariance matrix for the proposal distribution used in the random walk sampler. Default: diag(c(0.1, 0.1)).

n_steps

Integer. Number of MCMC steps to perform (default: 1000).

n_chains

Integer. Number of independent MCMC chains to run (default: 1).

n_particles

Integer. Number of particles to use in the particle filter and simulation (default: 1).

Value

A named list with the following components:

samples

Output of monty_sample, including sampled parameters and log-likelihoods.

posterior

The constructed posterior object (prior + likelihood) used in the fit.

all_states

Full simulation output unpacked from dust_unpack_state.

plots

List of ggplot plots: trace, loglik, combined, and sero.

Details

The function initializes two model trajectories: one with the default parameters and one with the MAP (maximum a posteriori) values. Serosurvey observations are matched by time and plotted alongside model predictions for visual validation.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
params <- PREVAIL::custom_data_process_wrapper(iso = "KEN", disease = "measles", R0 = 15)
serodata <- data.frame(time = 2500, serosurvey = I(list(rep(0.85, 17))))
fit <- fit_transmission_model(parameters = params, serodata = serodata, n_steps = 500)
fit$plots$combined
fit$plots$sero
} # }
